subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should `sessions_spawn` select only operator-declared lane profiles, and must every profile remain subordinate to one aggregate sub-agent concurrency budget?
rationale: This determines whether models may create new resource pools, how the existing global limit remains authoritative, and whether isolation can be added without enabling cost or availability bypasses.

options.title: Declared profiles with aggregate cap
options.body: Allow only configured lane profiles, retain `subagent` as the default, and enforce both profile-specific and aggregate sub-agent limits.

options.title: Derive isolation from target agents
options.body: Avoid a caller-selected lane and instead apply concurrency policies based on configured target-agent identities or roles.

options.title: Allow dynamic named lanes
options.body: Permit arbitrary caller-created lanes with independent limits, accepting a substantially larger resource-control and configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Declared profiles with aggregate cap
recommendation.body: Allow only configured lane profiles, retain `subagent` as the default, and enforce both profile-specific and aggregate sub-agent limits.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor is most directly connected to the original tool and concurrency behavior and has already participated in this issue's design review.
